claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations feature lets component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component state migrations are new (recently introduced).
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion for component state migrations feedback exists at https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
The legacy AWSX VPC component manages the VPC, subnets, route tables, and gateways.
The pulumi/examples repo contains an aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration example with v1, v2, and v3 programs and migration code.

In the example's v1, the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway, with a security group outside the component referring to the VPC.
Replacing an AWS VPC means the security group that refers to the VPC's ID must also be replaced (per the AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
If a database is recreated, its replacement does not automatically contain the old data; without a backup or data migration, deleting the old database could lose that data.
The example's third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

The Pulumi resource trees in the example are: v1 has awsx:x:ec2:Vpc with awsx:x:ec2:Subnet and awsx:x:ec2:InternetGateway component children; v2 has awsx:ec2:Vpc with aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc as child and subnet named vpc-isolated-1; v3 has plain aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc at the root.
Pulumi's state records both physical resources and components; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud-provider ID such as an AWS VPC ID.

Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts managed resources under different parents; in the example the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but do not remove component wrappers or transfer references to replacement resources.
Pulumi component resources accept a `stateMigrations` option that registers a migration callback, used together with an alias for the legacy component type.
The example's migration file exists at aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration/v2/migration.ts and defines `migrateClassicVpc`.

A state migration callback receives the aliased old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each old URN that disappears to the URN that replaces it).
In the example's first migration, the callback is idempotent: if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources it does nothing, and an unexpected component type raises an error.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent while preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.

Successor mappings returned by a migration let the Pulumi engine update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, so the security group's reference to the VPC remains valid and connected to the migrated VPC record with the same AWS VPC ID.
The example's third version declares the VPC, subnet, route table, association, and internet gateway directly with `@pulumi/aws`.

The example's second migration (v3/migration.ts) removes the AWSX VPC component record and moves the managed VPC into its place; both the old component and its VPC child map to the new VPC record, and the VPC keeps its AWS ID.
The plain VPC registration keeps aliases for both previous component types (legacy and modern AWSX) and both migration callbacks.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration, and once both have run the callbacks return no result on later updates.
Keeping earlier migrations with the component lets its users skip versions without editing stack state by hand.

After a migration changes saved state, Pulumi compares the new program with that state and calls the provider for any remaining changes; in this example the preview can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` before each upgrade should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.

When a component registers its migration in its implementation, users do not need to write the migration, attach the callback, or edit stack state; Pulumi runs the migration as part of the normal preview and update.
For an internal component change that keeps the same inputs and outputs, users can keep their existing component calls without needing to know which resources moved.
A component state migrations guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ and covers the callback contract.
Pulumi components page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/components/ and aliases page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/aliases/.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite resource state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN that is omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.

Pulumi component state migration state entries use the checkpoint resource format documented in the Pulumi developer docs deployment schema, including fields such as `urn`, `type`, `id`, `parent`, `provider`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.

A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates, and the restrictions on state-changing results do not require removing an already-applied migration.
